title: A study of MZE782 in adults with phenylketonuria
official: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Dose-ranging Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of MZE782 in Adults with Phenylketonuria (PKU)
summary:
Main objective: 1. To characterize the effect of MZE782 on plasma Phe concentrations over the 4-week DBPC Treatment Period in adults with PKU who have baseline plasma Phe levels >600 μMol/L.
2. To characterize the safety and tolerability of MZE782 in adults with PKU.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Is 18 to 75 years of age inclusive at the time of signing the informed consent.
2. 10. Is willing and able to comply with study procedures.
3. 11. Is capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Section 10.3, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in this protocol.
4. 12. Has had at least one Phe result (dried blood spot testing acceptable) obtained within 9 months (inclusive) prior to screening.
5. 13 Primary Cohorts – Cohorts 1A and 1B: If previously treated with pegvaliase, sepiapterin, or sapropterin, must agree to discontinue use during screening and refrain from using these medications until after the SFU Visit or ETV, if applicable. The following minimum washout periods are required prior to the first plasma Phe draw during screening: a. At least 14 days for those taking sapropterin or sepiapterin b. At least 28 days for those taking pegvaliase
6. 14. Primary Cohorts – Cohorts 1A and 1B:  Has an average result of >600 μMol/L from 2 plasma Phe results collected at least 7 days apart during the Screening Period
7. 15. Primary Cohorts – Cohorts 1A and 1B: Has at least one documented plasma Phe level  of >600 μMol/L (dried blood spot testing acceptable) over the past 2 years.
8. 16. Exploratory Cohort – Cohort 2 : Has been on a stable dose of a BH4 agent (ie, sapropterin or sepiapterin) for at least 12 weeks prior to screening (and has not received treatment with pegvaliase during this time).
9. 17. Exploratory Cohort – Cohort 2: Willing and able to stay on same stable dose of a BH4 agent throughout study.
10. 18. Exploratory Cohort – Cohort 2: Has an average result of >360 μmol/L from 2 plasma Phe results collected at least 7 days apart during the Screening Period
11. 19. Exploratory Cohort – Cohort 2:Has at least one documented plasma Phe level  of >360 μMol/L (dried blood spot testing acceptable) over the past 2 years.
12. 2. Has a minimum total body weight of 40.0 kg.
13. 3. Has clinical diagnosis of PKU.
14. 4. Is willing and able to maintain a consistent total dietary protein intake, including protein from both natural intact food sources and medical food products, according to the protocol throughout the duration of the study and under the supervision of a study dietitian or adequately trained designee per Investigator discretion, and intermittently keep an accurate food Diet Diary when required by the protocol
15. 5. If applicable, medication received for attention-deficient/hyperactivity disorder, depression, or other psychiatric disorders is stable (dose and frequency), and the condition has been adequately controlled for a minimum of 3 months prior to screening.
16. 6. If previously treated with LNAAs, must agree to discontinue use during screening and refrain from using until after the SFU Visit or ETV, if applicable. A 2-day minimum washout is required prior to the first plasma Phe draw during screening.
17. 7. Female participants of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test at the Screening Visit and a negative urine or serum pregnancy test at Day 1, prior to dosing with study intervention.
18. 8. Negative tests for hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb), hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus antibody at screening. a. Participants with positive HCV antibody are allowed if HCV RNA polymerase chain reaction is negative at screening. b. Participants with evidence of resolved hepatitis B virus infection and immunity (HBcAb+, HBsAg–, and hepatitis B surface antibody [HBsAb+]) are allowed.
19. 9. Participant agrees to the following based on sex assigned at birth. a. Male participants: Male participants are eligible to participate if they agree to the following during the study intervention period and for at least 90 days after the last dose of study intervention: • Refrain from donating sperm. •Use contraception/barrier as follows: -Use a male condom with female partners of childbearing potential who are also using a highly effective contraceptive method as defined in Appendix 3.  • Or, if not using contraception/barrier as per above, remain abstinent (if this is their consistent and preferred lifestyle). b. Female participants: A female participant is eligible to participate if she is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and one of the following conditions applies: • Is a female of non-childbearing potential as defined in Appendix 3, OR • Is a female of childbearing potential and using one of the accepted, highly effective contraceptive methods listed in Appendix 3, OR • Complete abstinence from heterosexual intercourse, if this is the participant’s consistent and preferred lifestyle. In addition, female participants must: • Agree to abstain from egg donation until 90 days after administration of the last dose of study intervention.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Has any condition that in the opinion of the Investigator would interfere with the evaluation of the study intervention or lead to increased risk of harm or that, in the view of the Investigator, places the participant at high risk of poor study intervention compliance or of not completing the study.
2. 10. Has total bilirubin ≥1.5 × ULN at screening (exception: participants with elevated total bilirubin may be included if the elevation is attributable to Gilbert syndrome, provided that direct bilirubin is within normal limits and there is no clinical or laboratory evidence of hepatic dysfunction),   OR aspartate transaminase or alanine transaminase ≥2 × ULN (if thought to be likely transient by the Investigator [for example, due to strenuous exercise], may be retested once during the Screening Period at the discretion of the Investigator).
3. 11. Has had an organ or bone marrow transplantation.
4. 12. Has ongoing alcohol or substance abuse as determined by the Investigator.
5. 13. Has used any investigational drug within 30 days or < 5  half ‑ lives of the investigational product, whichever is longer, prior to the Screening Visit.
6. 14. Hypersensitivity to MZE782 or any components of the study intervention.
7. 15. Is unable to tolerate oral medication or to swallow tablets.
8. 16. Received >50 mL of blood or plasma within 30 days of screening or >500 mL of blood or plasma within 60 days of screening.
9. 2. Diagnosed with an inborn error of BH4 metabolism.
10. 3. Females who are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed during the study.
11. 4. Females or males who plan to conceive/become pregnant during the study or within 90  days (females) or 90  days (males) after the last dose of study intervention.
12. 5. History of cancer within the past 2 years, with the exception of successfully treated non‑melanoma skin cancer, stage 0 cervical cancer, or stage 1 prostate cancer.
13. 6. History of vasculitis or other autoimmune/inflammatory disorders affecting the vasculature.
14. 7. Has a clinically significant elevation of C-reactive protein (CRP) or fibrinogen above the upper limit of normal (ULN) at screening that, in the opinion of the Investigator, and in consultation with the Sponsor Medical Monitor, is suggestive of an active inflammatory process or could otherwise confound interpretation of safety findings during the study. If the elevation is considered attributable to a transient, self-limited condition, the affected analyte(s) should be retested during the Screening Period on up to 2 additional occasions and must be within normal limits for eligibility.
15. 8. Clinically significant abnormal screening ECG, including but not limited to, corrected QT interval using Fridericia’s formula (QTcF) >450 ms or history of QT interval prolongation
16. 9. Has an estimated glomerular filtration rate based on cystatin C (eGFRcys) <45 mL/min/1.73 m² at screening. Note: eGFRcys will be calculated as described in Appendix 2.
